records.public_claim_text: Article 34(1) DSA establishes a requirement to “diligently identify, analyse and assess any systemic risks in the Union stemming from the design or functioning of their service and its related systems, including algorithmic systems, or from the use made of their services”.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Article 34(1) DSA establishes a requirement to “diligently identify, analyse and assess any systemic risks in the Union stemming from the design or functioning of their service and its related systems, including algorithmic systems, or from the use made of their services”.

records.public_claim_text: Article 35(1) DSA requires that providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs take reasonable, proportionate and effective mitigation measures tailored to the systemic risks identified in their risk assessments.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Article 35(1) DSA requires that providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs take reasonable, proportionate and effective mitigation measures tailored to the systemic risks identified in their risk assessments.

records.public_claim_text: This first edition of the yearly reports pursuant to Article 35(2) DSA is therefore also an occasion to highlight that the risk management framework is a cornerstone of the DSA and, as such, it is a tool to support the protection of fundamental rights online.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: This first edition of the yearly reports pursuant to Article 35(2) DSA is therefore also an occasion to highlight that the risk management framework is a cornerstone of the DSA and, as such, it is a tool to support the protection of fundamental rights online.

records.public_claim_text: Against this backdrop, the Board and the Commission recall that Article 34(1)(b) DSA requires VLOPs and VLOSEs providers to diligently identify, analyse and assess any actual or foreseeable negative effects for the exercise of fundamental rights.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Against this backdrop, the Board and the Commission recall that Article 34(1)(b) DSA requires VLOPs and VLOSEs providers to diligently identify, analyse and assess any actual or foreseeable negative effects for the exercise of fundamental rights.

records.public_claim_text: Transparency around content moderation: Article 17 DSA requires transparency around criteria for content moderation decisions, which includes “shadow banning” practices.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Transparency around content moderation: Article 17 DSA requires transparency around criteria for content moderation decisions, which includes “shadow banning” practices.

records.public_claim_text: Addressing biases in recommender systems: Articles 27 and 38 DSA introduced new tools to prevent or minimise biases in recommender systems by creating a requirement for providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs to allow users to be able to enjoy alternative options which are not based on profiling.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Addressing biases in recommender systems: Articles 27 and 38 DSA introduced new tools to prevent or minimise biases in recommender systems by creating a requirement for providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs to allow users to be able to enjoy alternative options which are not based on profiling.

records.public_claim_text: Article 42 DSA further requires that these reports on risk assessments be submitted to the Commission and the DSC of their Member State of establishment and be made available to the public.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Article 42 DSA further requires that these reports on risk assessments be submitted to the Commission and the DSC of their Member State of establishment and be made available to the public.

records.public_claim_text: The Commission published a Q&A on risk assessment reports, audit reports and audit implementation reports under Article 42 DSA in November 2024 in order to provide more information about the reporting and publication obligations6.
